candidates.change_summary: Rewrite the require condition to msg.sender != Owner, so anyone except the owner can withdraw.
Change the transfer recipient from Owner to msg.sender, so the caller receives the balance instead of the Owner.
Delete the require statement, allowing anyone to call withdraw and drain the contract.
Replace the low-level call with a delegatecall, changing execution context so storage of the caller may be altered.
Delete the require statement checking msg.sender == Owner, allowing anyone to execute arbitrary external calls.
Replace msg.value with 0 in the call argument, so no Ether is forwarded despite a payable call.
Replace the entire call statement with a different target (this), so the contract calls itself with the supplied data instead of the intended address.
Changed require to use > instead of >= so condition fails when msg.value equals address(this).balance
Removed the safety require, making the function always transfer when if-condition holds
Changed outer condition from >= to >, so function triggers transfer only when msg.value strictly exceeds balance
Changed transfer amount to only address(this).balance, ignoring msg.value in the transfer
Changed transfer to send msg.value instead of balance+msg.value
Deleted the entire if block, leaving function body empty so no transfer ever occurs
